data.body_html:
When planning a Marbella boat rental, deciding between Sotogrande and Estepona marinas can shape your entire day on the water. Both offer distinct experiences, from dining and activities to atmosphere and proximity to Puerto Banús. This guide breaks down the key differences so you can choose the best stop for your charter. All our boats depart from Puerto Banús, making either destination an easy cruise away.

Location and Distance from Puerto Banús

Estepona Marina lies just 5 nautical miles east of Puerto Banús — a 15-20 minute cruise at 20 knots. Sotogrande is further west at 12 nautical miles, a 30-40 minute trip. If you're short on time, Estepona is the quicker option. For a longer day out, Sotogrande offers a more exclusive setting. Our Marbella boat rental fleet includes fast boats like the Mangusta 80 that can cover these distances comfortably.

Dining and Restaurants

Estepona Marina boasts a lively promenade with over 20 restaurants and bars, from casual tapas at La Escollera to fine dining at El Faro. Sotogrande is more upscale, featuring the Sotogrande Yacht Club and Michelin-starred options like Restaurante Sollo. For a relaxed lunch with sea views, Estepona wins on variety. For a special evening, Sotogrande's exclusivity is hard to beat.

Activities and Attractions

Estepona offers sandy beaches, a water park (Aqualand), and paddleboarding rentals. Sotogrande is a golfer's paradise with several top-ranked courses, plus sailing schools and kite surfing. Both have beach clubs — Estepona's Beach Club Atalaya is popular, while Sotogrande's La Reserva Club is more private. Your charter can include a stop at either for swimming or water sports.

Atmosphere and Crowds

Estepona is vibrant and family-friendly, with a busy promenade and a mix of tourists and locals. Sotogrande is quieter and more exclusive, attracting a wealthier crowd seeking privacy and luxury. If you want a lively day out, choose Estepona. For a serene escape, Sotogrande is ideal.

Marina Facilities

Estepona Marina has 200 berths, showers, and a small shopping area. Sotogrande Marina has 350 berths, a yacht club, and luxury boutiques. Both offer fuel docks and repair services, but Sotogrande's facilities are more comprehensive for larger yachts over 20 metres. Our boats like the Ferretti 94 (29m) can berth at either with advance booking.

Cost and Booking

Berthing fees at Estepona are generally lower than Sotogrande, which can charge premium rates for its exclusive status. For a day trip, many charters simply anchor in the bay rather than mooring. Our Marbella boat rental Sotogrande vs Estepona guide includes tips on booking berths. All our charters include a licensed skipper who can advise on the best anchorage.

Which Marina Should You Choose?

If you want quick access, lively dining, and family activities, Estepona is the better choice. For a luxurious, quiet day with golf or exclusive clubs, Sotogrande wins. Both are easily reachable from Puerto Banús on any of our boats. For a 2-hour charter, Estepona is more practical; for a full day, Sotogrande offers a more memorable experience. Estepona Marina is approximately 15 minutes by car from Puerto Banús, while Sotogrande is around 30 minutes west. By boat, both are easily reachable within a 20-40 minute cruise depending on speed and conditions.

Which marina has better dining options for a boat charter stop?

Estepona Marina has a more vibrant dining scene with over 20 restaurants and bars along its promenade, offering everything from tapas to fine dining. Sotogrande is more exclusive, with upscale spots like the Sotogrande Yacht Club and several Michelin-starred options.

Can I anchor my charter boat at Sotogrande or Estepona?

Both marinas have visitor berths, but space can be limited in peak season. It's best to book ahead through your skipper. Alternatively, you can anchor in the bay off Estepona or near the Sotogrande river mouth, though conditions vary.

Which marina is better for families on a Marbella boat rental?

Estepona is more family-friendly with its sandy beaches, a water park nearby, and a lively yet relaxed atmosphere. Sotogrande is quieter and more geared towards golf and luxury living, though it has a kids' club and beach club options.

Are there any water sports or activities near these marinas?

Estepona offers jet skiing, paddleboarding, and banana boat rides from its beach. Sotogrande is known for sailing schools, kite surfing, and paddle tennis. Both have options within easy reach of your charter boat.

What is the distance from Puerto Banús to Estepona and Sotogrande by boat?

From Puerto Banús, Estepona is about 5 nautical miles east (15-20 minutes at 20 knots). Sotogrande is roughly 12 nautical miles west (30-40 minutes at 25 knots). Our Mangusta 80 can cover this quickly.

Which marina has the best nightlife for a sunset cruise?

Estepona has a more varied nightlife with beach bars and clubs along the promenade, ideal for after-dinner drinks. Sotogrande is more subdued, with a focus on exclusive lounges and private events at the yacht club.
